_about: Answers shaped like the Grok agents' replies for a 'Data Engineering' career guide, written for offline tests. No real people: the posts use role descriptions, not names or handles.

career_plan.title: Data Engineer
career_plan.oneLine: Builds the pipelines and storage that move raw data to analysts and models.

angles.basics: Batch and streaming pipelines, SQL and Python, warehouses such as Snowflake or BigQuery, orchestration with Airflow, and data modelling.
angles.voices: Junior and senior data engineers, analytics engineers, and people who moved in from analyst or software roles.
angles.interview: SQL screens, Python coding rounds, data modelling and pipeline design interviews, and behavioural rounds.
angles.start: SQL first, then Python, one end-to-end pipeline project, and a cloud fundamentals course, ready for the SQL and design rounds.

career_basics.summary: Data engineers design, build and run the pipelines that collect, clean and store data so analysts and machine learning teams can use it.
dayInLife: Check overnight pipeline runs and fix a failed job
Write a SQL model for a new dashboard
Meet analysts about a new data source
whatTheyDo: Keep storage and compute costs down

specialties.name: Analytics engineering
specialties.what: SQL models and tests that analysts build on

specialties.name: Streaming
specialties.what: Real-time pipelines on Kafka or Kinesis

specialties.name: Platform engineering
specialties.what: The shared tools other data engineers use

career_basics.education: Usually a bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems or a related field.

pay.figure: Median about $135,000 a year in the US (2025)

career_basics.outlook: Faster than average growth as more companies move data to the cloud.

posts.author: A senior data engineer
posts.role: Senior data engineer at a payments company
posts.text: Most of my week is not writing new pipelines. It is making old ones reliable and cheaper.
posts.takeaway: Learn monitoring and testing, not only building.

posts.author: A junior data engineer
posts.text: I got the job because my portfolio had one pipeline that ran every day, with tests and a README.
posts.takeaway: One working, scheduled project beats five notebooks.

posts.author: An analytics engineer
posts.text: SQL is still 80% of the job. Get really good at window functions.

career_voices_summary.summary: People say the work is mostly keeping pipelines reliable and cheap. They advise strong SQL and one scheduled, tested project.

formats.name: SQL screen
formats.tests: Joins, aggregations and window functions under time
formats.howToPractice: Timed problems on a practice site, then explain each query aloud

formats.name: Pipeline design interview
formats.tests: How you would move and model data for a product
formats.howToPractice: Sketch three pipelines end to end and talk through failure cases

formats.name: Behavioural interview
formats.tests: Ownership and how you handle broken data
formats.howToPractice: Write four short stories about problems you fixed

questions.question: Find each customer's second most recent order.
questions.tip: Use ROW_NUMBER over a partition and say why not a self-join.

questions.question: Design a pipeline for click events that analysts can query within an hour.
questions.tip: Start from the consumers and the freshness they need.

questions.question: Tell me about a time data you owned was wrong.
questions.tip: Say how you found it, fixed it, and stopped it happening again.

steps.title: Learn SQL to window functions
steps.detail: Work through joins, grouping and window functions on a real dataset.

steps.title: Build one scheduled pipeline
steps.detail: Load a public dataset daily with Airflow, test it, and write a README.

steps.title: Write four problem stories
steps.detail: One per project: what broke, what you did, what changed.
